questions.q: What is the chance performance level and how was it computed?
questions.answer: Sec. 2.4: 32 blocks of 425 trials on white Gaussian noise; mean 46.2% (2.7% SD). Earlier reader answer corrected by the writer from the Sec. 2.4 passage.

questions.q: How many closed-loop trials did each patient complete?
questions.answer: Sec. 2.4: 98, 139, 61 and 69 trials (Patients 1-4). Earlier reader answer corrected.

questions.q: Was there a train/validation split for feature selection during screening?
questions.answer: Not described. Screening used all data for r² calculation between conditions; no cross-validation or held-out set mentioned for feature selection.

questions.q: What were the autoregressive model parameters for spectral estimation?
questions.answer: Not specified. Only 'autoregressive spectral estimation in 2 Hz bins ranging from 0 to 550 Hz' stated; model order, window length, taper not given.

questions.q: Were the same electrodes/features used across overt and imagined conditions for Patient 3?
questions.answer: Paper states topographical and frequency distributions 'were often distinct between real and imagined phoneme articulation' for Patient 3, implying different features.

questions.q: What is the exact microgrid configuration for Patient 2?
questions.answer: 16 microwires, 75 μm diameter, 1 mm spacing, placed over dorsal premotor cortex (BA 6) outside clinical grid.

questions.q: Did any patient achieve control on the first closed-loop session without prior BCI training?
questions.answer: Yes: "two of our four patients immediately had greater that 90% accuracy without any prior training" (Sec. 4). Patients 1 (91%) and likely Patient 3 (73%) or 4 (69%) were the rapid learners.

questions.q: Were covert trials monitored for overt movement or sound (EMG, microphone, video)?
questions.answer: No monitoring is described in Secs. 2.2-2.4 (writer grep of target text for EMG/microphone/audio/mouth: no hits on monitoring).

questions.q: Which earlier BCI designs does the target itself cite for speech-related control tasks?
questions.answer: Sec. 4: earlier ECoG BCIs used tongue movements and articulation of single words (Schalk 2008a, Leuthardt 2004); Sec. 1: Wilson 2006 auditory cortex cursor control.

questions.q: Fig. 8: early-block and last-block accuracies per patient?
questions.answer: Writer read Fig. 8 (PMC figure image): see t66. Patients 1-2 start at about 88-90%; Table 2 values do not match the last points for Patients 1, 3, 4.
